intro_html: This is the humble Cantonese rice plate: seasoned minced meat in a glossy brown gravy, spooned over rice with peas stirred through. The gravy is the whole reason it belongs in a meal prep rotation, because sauce is what keeps lean turkey from turning into cardboard by Thursday. Each bowl lands at 567 calories and 31 grams of protein for about $3.04 (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $3.04 a bowl (at everyday cost). Rice, turkey, peas, and a gravy built from a bottle of oyster sauce you already own. That is a Tuesday dinner solved, fourteen times over.
shop_smart: Oyster sauce and soy sauce carry all the flavor here for very little, and both bottles keep for months. Once your pantry has them, dinners like this stop requiring a shopping trip.
Frozen peas cost almost nothing for this batch and add color, sweetness, and a little fiber. They are the most useful bag in your freezer and they never spoil on you.
Cornstarch is what turns broth into gravy, and it costs almost nothing for the whole batch. It is the cheapest ingredient in the store that changes a dish this much.
The turkey is well over half the cost, so buy the 4 pound pack. Everything else on this list is measured in cents.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide skillet over medium-high, add the ground turkey, and brown it, breaking it into fine crumbles, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Add the diced onion and minced garlic and cook 4 minutes until the onion softens and goes translucent.
Pour in the chicken broth, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and black pepper, and bring it to a simmer for 5 minutes so the flavors settle in together.
Whisk the cornstarch with a half cup of cold water until smooth. Cold water, always, since cornstarch in hot liquid turns into lumps you cannot whisk out.
Stir the slurry into the simmering pan and cook 2 minutes until the sauce turns glossy and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Add the frozen peas and the sesame oil and cook 2 minutes more, just until the peas are hot and still bright green.
Cook the rice, move it into your weighed pot, and keep the gravy in its own pan for portioning.
portion_html: Set the pot of rice on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. That is the rice bed for each container. Then ladle the gravy evenly over all 14, stirring between scoops so the meat does not sink and leave the last few containers swimming in plain sauce. Each bowl lands at 567 calories and 31 grams of protein.

steps: Brown the ground turkey in vegetable oil to 165F.
Add onion and garlic and cook 4 minutes.
Add chicken broth, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and pepper and simmer 5 minutes.
Whisk cornstarch with cold water and stir it in to thicken the gravy.
Add frozen peas and sesame oil and cook 2 minutes.
Cook the rice, portion by weight into 14 containers, and ladle the gravy over the top.
